findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The bar hand washing sink was obstructed by the garbage can. CORRECTED- the can was moved. Find a new placement for the trash can that does not block the sink. Hand washing sinks must be maintained accessible at all times to allow for hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the baffles of the ice machine to contain an accumulation of soil debris. CORRECTED- The ice was covered, and baffles were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination of consumables.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing freezer upstairs to be in disrepair. The current handle is corner trim and duct tape. Duct tape is an adhesive, and therefore deteriorates. Discussed applying a sheet metal with a convex handle. CORRECTED- the duct tape was removed.  All nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed chemical sanitizing dish machine to be dispensing 0 ppm Cl. CORRECTED- the dish machine was primed and re-run until 50 ppm Cl was observed. Ensure frequent testing of sanitizer concentration with test strips to ensure proper sanitation of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing freezer upstairs to be in disrepair. The handle had been broken off and replaced with a pool noodle and scotch tape. The PIC stated that they are working on ordering a replacement part. Ensure equipment is maintained in repair. All nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items within the physical facility in need of repair. 
1) The floor drain cover in front of the dish machine is missing.
2) Caulking behind the triple sink is fragmented. 
Ensure these items are replaced and resealed by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
All three Allergen certificates on file were observed to have expired last year. High risk establishments are required to have Allergen training for their Certified Food Protection Managers. Ensure managers retake the Allergen course by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed 3 soup ladles hanging in ready to use position behind cheese sauce hot holding in kitchen to contain soil accumulation. CORRECTED- ladles were taken to the triple sink to be cleaned and sanitized before use. Ensure utensils that are stored in ready to use position are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. [P]

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a contained of white powder (identified as flour) above the pizza station at the end of the kitchen. CORRECTED-person in charge was notified and the flour was voluntarily discarded. Ensure white powders and other items that can be mistaken for others are labeled after they are removed from their original container.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a 2 oz. plastic container submerged in flour being stored on the shelf above the pizza station. CORRECTED- person in charge discarded the contents of the entire container (see violation #37). Use scoops with handles directed outwards, outside of the food to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing cooler upstairs to be in disrepair. The handle had been broken off and replaced with a pool noodle and scotch tape. Inspector notified the person in charge so that the equipment can be repaired. Ensure equipment is maintained in repair.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed soil accumulation along the gasket perimeter of the chest freezers upstairs. CORRECTED- the person in charge wiped the gaskets with a clean sanitizer rag. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the facility in need of physical repair;
1) There is a hole in the ceiling upstairs above the soda boxes. This may be indicative of water damage. The inspector notified the person in charge of this damage, so that it may be repaired by the next routine inspection.
2) The mop sink at the entry of the kitchen was observed to have degraded caulking between the sink and the wall. The area between the mop sink basin and wall should be cleaned and either repaired or replaced.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good condition.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Buttermilk observed in the cook-line prep cooler was out of date per the manufacturer’s label. PIC was informed and the buttermilk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff discarding any out of date items.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Shell eggs were observed to be stored in a prep cooler below raw beef slider patties. Raw eggs should be stored above raw ground meat, but below fresh produce and other ready-to-eat foods. PIC was informed of incorrect storage, and eggs were moved to the walk-in cooler. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Fourteen bottles of Simply brand orange juice were observed stored on an ambient shelf in dry storage. The bottles are marked “keep refrigerated,” and the Coca-Cola website states that the Simply branded juices contain no preservatives, and therefore require refrigeration at all times. Juices were discarded. Violation is considered corrected on site.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Peeled hard-boiled eggs were observed stored in water in both the prep cooler and walk-in cooler. Storing eggs in water presents an unnecessary risk of cross-contamination. PIC was informed that eggs should be kept in a food-safe container free of ice or water.
findings.citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: 1st REPEAT: Two of the storage chest freezers upstairs have damage to the interior of the lid, creating cracks and crevices. Repair the cooler lids so the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The chest freezers upstairs were observed to be soiled with mold around the sides of the lids and lid seals. PIC was informed that chest freezers are in need of a deep clean. Ensure chest freezers are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent mold accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The flooring in the upstairs dry storage area was observed to be in disrepair. The floors are cracked, bubbled, and wearing thin. This makes it difficult to properly clean the floors, posing the risk of cross-contamination. Ensure floors are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The floors in the outdoor walk-in cooler were observed to be soiled with food debris. Ensure staff are cleaning floors of coolers often enough to avoid accumulation of food debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw shell eggs observed stored above thawing vegetables in the bottom of the short prep cooler. CORRECTED- Storage was rearranged to store vegetables above eggs. Ensure foods are stored to prevent potential cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Six (1 gal) containers of cheese sauce, in the walk-in cooler and labeled indicating cooling began at 10am, were observed at 104-136F (probed). Four containers were observed at 104F to 109F, and were voluntarily discarded. Two containers, observed at 135F and 136F, were kept to be cooled. Upon returning to the kitchen, staff explained that they had mismarked the time cooling began. Ensure foods are cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours, and are cooled from 135F to 41F within 6 hours. Keep logs to show that foods are being cooled properly and that the process is being monitored. 
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Thermometers were not found in several coolers on the cookline. Ensure ambient air thermometers are present in all cold holding units. CORRECTED- PIC found thermometers upstairs and added them to each of the cookline coolers.
4-204.112: (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
One of the storage chest freezers upstairs has damage to the interior of the lid, creating cracks and crevices. Repair the cooler lid so the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
4-202.16: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. [C]
